chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', Abu Sayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I dislike for my community that a man should have intercourse with his wife during the middle of the month or at the beginning of the crescent, for the rebellious devils and Jinn overwhelm the children of Adam, causing them to become insane and deranged. Do you not see that the afflicted ones suffer epileptic fits during the middle of the month and at the beginning of the crescent?'
ai.seo_question: Why is intimacy discouraged during the middle of the lunar month in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), linking the spiritual vulnerability of the Ummah to the increased activity of Maradat al-Shaytan (rebellious devils) during the middle of the lunar month and the new moon. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on aligning physical acts with cosmic rhythms, suggesting that avoiding intimacy during these peak times of spiritual turbulence preserves mental clarity and prevents 'Junnun' (a state of spiritual or physical derangement). The reference to epilepsy serves as a tangible sign of this unseen influence, reinforcing the practical wisdom of regulating marital relations for holistic well-being.

en.hubeali:
Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a Abu Sayyar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘I<sup>saww</sup> dislike it for my<sup>saww</sup> community that the man sleeps with his wife during the middle of the month, or during the beginning of the crescent, for the rebellious devils and the Jinn overwhelm the children of Adam<sup>as</sup>, so they are becoming insane and deranged. Are you not seeing the ones afflicted ones having epileptic fits during the middle of the month and during the beginning of the cresecent?’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Safwan from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said
the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is detestable for a man to go to bed with his wife in the night of his arrival from a journey until the morning.’”
